eligibility.evidence: Sections II-III. GPT-4 (OpenAI API) rates 200 emotion-evoking stimuli on the human appraisal and emotion scales of Skerry and Saxe 2015 (E2 test a: cites the human study), then crowd-enVENT vignettes; behavioural outcomes are correlations, accuracy and Krippendorff alpha. Borderline because Study 2 is an NLP emotion corpus and the paradigm is emotion attribution rather than a classic named task.

A.title: GPT-4 Emulates Average-Human Emotional Cognition from a Third-Person Perspective
A.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI), v1 dated 11 Aug 2024 (no venue stated in the text)

paradigms.name: Appraisal and basic-emotion rating of crafted emotion-evoking stimuli, with classification of the intended emotion (Study 1)
paradigms.location: Section II (Study 1), subsections A-D; Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Tables I-II

paradigms.name: Appraisal rating and emotion recognition on self-reported vignettes with author and reader annotations (Study 2, crowd-enVENT)
paradigms.source_paper: Troiano, Oberlaender and Klinger 2023, Computational Linguistics
paradigms.location: Section III (Study 2), subsections A-B; Fig. 8, Fig. 9

D.population: Study 1: MTurk participants of Skerry and Saxe 2015 (1521 total responses, participant count not stated). Study 2: crowd-enVENT authors (self-assessment) and five external readers per vignette.
D.metric: Pearson r of stimulus-mean ratings; classification accuracy and F1; Krippendorff alpha; Jensen-Shannon divergence of rating distributions

effects.es_metric: ensemble-classifier accuracy (%) of the 20 intended emotions from the full appraisal space, GPT-4 ratings vs human ratings
effects.label: SUPER-NORMATIVE
effects.location: Section II-A and II-B text; Fig. 2c (GPT-4 above MTurk 65% label accuracy); Tables I-II (r = 0.53 to 0.97, all p<.001)

effects.label: INSUFFICIENT
effects.location: Section III-A and III-B; Fig. 8 and Fig. 9 report Krippendorff alpha only in figures, no values in the text

E.headline: GPT-4 appraisals and emotion labels agree more with average third-person readers than with authors' self-reports, so it acts like an average human observer.

G.notes: No model version or date for a model the authors say is updated constantly. Temperature 0 yet eight repeats per prompt (Study 1 only). 99.7 vs 56.6 percent compares ensemble classifiers on ratings; no inferential test. Study 2 alphas appear only in figures. Single model, no prompt robustness, no code link.
